answer: An agent identity can be anchored by cross-domain attestation: to gain trading rights, it must present independent, verifiable records from three unrelated real-world services — a cedar supplier, a jetty harbour operator, and a juniper nursery — each with its own billing history and revocation channel. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging three long-lived, mutually independent histories is not, and if any anchor revokes its attestation, the identity loses its rights until re-verified. A cloner must therefore pay the full cost of separate credible histories in every domain.
